articles.title: How these notes age
articles.summary: Publication, editing, review, and expiry are different events. Here is how to read their dates.
articles.author: Jean Marin

visual.title: Three different clocks
visual.caption: An edit changes the edit date. Only a technical review changes the review date. Neither resets the age of a news report.

sections.title: News has a defined lifetime
paragraphs: News and magazine editions describe information available at a known time. After three calendar months, the site labels them Outdated news and moves them out of the current listing. The archive remains accessible.
A later edit does not renew that news window. A materially new report gets a new dated entry and links to the earlier one.

sections.title: Guides need review
paragraphs: A guide explains knowledge that can remain useful for longer. Its last technical review and next review date are visible. The default proposed review period is six months. Fast-changing instructions use three months.
Review due means the planned check has not been recorded. It does not prove the content is wrong. Known errors require an immediate correction or warning.

sections.title: Experiments keep their context
paragraphs: An experiment is a record of one test setup. It keeps the test date, product versions, method, results, and limitations. A dated result does not guarantee the same behavior in a newer release.

articles.title: Publication trial: from repository to public page
articles.summary: A clearly labelled test page for checking creation, deployment, and a later update.
articles.author: Jean Marin

visual.title: The release path
visual.caption: A commit starts a deployment. Publication is confirmed only after the deployed page is read and checked.

sections.title: A test, not a research article
paragraphs: This page tests the publication process. It contains no private research or client material. The current release marker is publication-test-v2. The first public release used publication-test-v1 and was checked before this update.

sections.title: What the check covers
paragraphs: The first stage checks that this page is accessible at its public address. A second release changes the marker. Reading the changed public page checks that updates also reach the website.
The catalogue and maintenance ledger are generated from the same article metadata. Every public page includes an explanatory visual.
